_comment: ADOPTER: the obligations register (2.1.0, hardening plan phase 3) — mounted as docs/governance/obligations.json and OWNED in CODEOWNERS by compliance or the second line. Until now the chain was free-text regulatory drivers → DR-* risk categories → CTRL-* controls → gates; nothing named the OBLIGATION itself, so 'show me every control for obligation X' had no answer. Each entry here is one obligation: where it comes from, which article, who owns keeping it current, when it was last verified against the source, the register risks and controls that answer it, and the FINOS SDLC draft mitigations it maps to. scripts/obligations-check.mjs fails an entry that resolves to no risk or no control, a stale last_verified, an owner nobody holds, or an unknown FINOS catalogue version. D6 requires a data-governance document to cite at least one OB-* id that resolves here; change-watch reports drift per obligation to its owner_role.
_illustrative_comment: EVERY ENTRY BELOW IS ILLUSTRATIVE (`illustrative: true`). They show the SHAPE — a plausible UAE set across consumer protection, personal data, model management, operational risk, outsourcing and AI — with the article field left as an ADOPT placeholder ON PURPOSE: regulatory figures and article numbers are load-bearing and are never paraphrased from memory into a control (CLAUDE.md). Under a regulated profile an illustrative entry FAILS the gate; replace each with your compliance function's verified entry (source, article, owner, date) or delete it. The real taxonomy is never committed to a shared repository: point `private_path` at a file outside the tree if your register cannot be public.

finos_catalogue.note: Draft identifiers; they will move. The loader refuses a ref it does not know, so a moved catalogue is a loud failure, not a silent mismatch.

obligations.source: CBUAE Operational Risk regulation and standards
obligations.title: Material incidents are reported to the regulator within the prescribed period
